prompt: We want our Gemini agent to both read knowledge articles AND create tickets in ServiceNow — except we use a fork of ServiceNow that isn't the native connector. How do I do this?

assertions.name: identifies_both_paths_needed
assertions.text: Identifies that BOTH paths are needed for this use case — an ingestion connector for the knowledge corpus and an MCP server for the write (create ticket) action.

assertions.name: explains_ingestion_readonly_constraint
assertions.text: Explains that ingestion connectors are read-only into the datastore and cannot write back to the source, which is why a write action requires an MCP server.

assertions.name: mcp_create_ticket_tool
assertions.text: Defines a create_ticket (or similar) MCP tool with a narrow, verb-led signature — not a generic write_anything tool.

assertions.name: ingestion_for_kb_corpus
assertions.text: Uses the ingestion connector pattern for the knowledge articles corpus so answers can be grounded with citations.

assertions.name: addresses_acl_for_kb
assertions.text: Addresses how ACLs map for the KB corpus — readers per article or idp_wide where appropriate.

assertions.name: addresses_auth_for_both
assertions.text: Addresses authentication for both paths — OAuth for the MCP server, and a service account or fetch-time credentials for the ingestion connector.

assertions.name: streamable_http_for_mcp
assertions.text: Specifies StreamableHTTP transport for the MCP server (not SSE).

assertions.name: stable_doc_ids
assertions.text: Uses stable document IDs from the ServiceNow KB article primary key in the ingestion connector.
